 Judgment

Being aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 23.07.2014 passed in MVC No.225/2010 by the learned Principal Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Mandya, whereby the petition filed by the petitioners came to be allowed in part, a sum of Rs.7,87,000/- has been awarded as compensation The Branch Manager vs Smt Lakshmamma on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169262750/
2 together with interest and directed the Insurance Company to deposit the same, the insurance company is before this Court in appeal urging various grounds.
2. The parties are referred to as per their nomenclature before the Tribunal for the sake of convenience.

3. The brief facts of the case are as below:
That on 9.8.2009, Chikkalingaiah and one Jayalingegowda were going towards Yeliyur village by walking on the left side of the road at about 11:30 a.m. and when they were going near Yeliyur Circle on Mysore- Bangalore road, Hero Honda Passion motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-09/EN-4671 being driven by its rider rashly &
negligently came from Mysore towards Mandya and dashed against Chikkalingaiah.
As a result, he fell down and sustained grievous injury to head and other parts of the body.
Immediately, he was admitted to Mandya District hospital and then to NIMHANS, Bangalore and then to Maharaja Agrasena hospital, Bangalore.
But inspite of treatment, he died on 19.9.2009 at 11:55 p.m. Post mortem on the dead body was conducted at Victoria hospital, Bangalore and thereafter, the dead body was handed over to petitioners.

The petitioners have contended that they spent Rs.20,000/- for taking the dead body to native place for cremation and Rs.50,000/-
for performing funeral and 11th day ceremony of their son and spent Rs.1,60,000/-
for medical expenses while he was inpatient in the hospital.
Further it is the case of petitioners that due to unfortunate death of their son, they have suffered mental shock and agony.

4. It is the further case of the petitioners that, deceased was aged 40 years at the time of accident and doing agriculture and milk vending business and earning Rs.8,000/- per month and used to spend his entire earnings for maintenance of the family.

After the death of deceased, 1st petitioner has lost the company of her husband at her young age and petitioners No.3, 4 & 5 have lost love and affection of their father and 2nd petitioner being aged mother has lost valuable assistance of her son in her old age and they have been put to much hardship and great injustice.
It is the further case of the petitioners that, the accident in question was exclusively due to rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Therefore, they claimed compensation of Rs.15,45,000/-.
5. On issuance of notice by the Tribunal, respondent Nos.1 and 2 both have appeared before the Tribunal through their respective counsels and filed their separate written statements.

6. The respondent No.1 in his objection statement admitted that a criminal case was registered against the driver of Hero Honda Passion bearing Reg.No.KA-09/EN 4671 by Mandya Rural Police Station and denied the relationship of petitioners with the deceased.

It is contended that the amount of compensation claimed by the petitioners is too high and exorbitant and he being owner of Hero Honda Passion bearing No.KA-09/EN-4671 has insured the vehicle with 2nd respondent and policy was in force as on the date of accident and the driver of the said vehicle was also having valid and The Branch Manager vs Smt Lakshmamma on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169262750/
3 effective DL to drive the vehicle. Hence, prayed to dismiss the petition.
7. Respondent No.2 in its written statement has denied the coverage of insurance with it on the date of accident.
It is contended that the owner of Hero Honda has not intimated about occurrence of accident immediately and thereby Sec.134 (c) of MV Act.
The quantum of compensation claimed is all false, imaginary, without any legal basis, as such petitioners are not entitled for the same.

It is also contended that the accident had happened on 9-8-2009 but the complaint was lodged on 11-8-2009 after the delay of two days and it indicates the collusion of the petitioners and the respondent No.1 to make a wrongful gain from respondent No.2.
Further it has contended that the driver of Hero Honda was not having valid driving license to drive the particular category of vehicle as on the date of accident.
Hence, prayed to dismiss the petition.

8. On the basis of the above pleadings and contentions of the parties, the Tribunal has framed necessary issues for its consideration and after considering the oral evidence of PWs-1 and 2 and RWs 1 and 2 and documentary evidence of Exs.P1 to 11 and Exs.R1 to R14 on behalf of both the parties, allowed the petition in part and directed the Insurance company to deposit the compensation of Rs.7,87,000/- under different heads as below:
 Loss of dependency Rs.5,67,000/-
 Towards medical expenses Rs.1,50,000/-
Towards transportation and funeral Rs. 15,000/- and 11th day ceremony expenses Towards loss of consortium Rs. 20,000/- Towards loss of Love and affection Rs. 20,000/-
 and also protection  Towards loss of estate Rs. 15,000/-
 Total Rs.7,87,000/-
9.

Being aggrieved by the same, the Insurance Company has approached this Court in this appeal seeking to set aside the same, contending that the finding of the Tribunal that the insured motor cycle was involved in the accident in the manner pleaded do suffer from illegalities and infirmities.
It is contended that the insured motor cycle was falsely implicated with active cooperation of the insured and the police.
Such implication was apparent with the complaints filed to SP Mandya and the statements of the witnesses recorded by the Police as well as the investigator of the insurer.
It is alleged that the claimant has not examined Jayalingegowda, who claimed to be with the deceased at the time of the alleged accident with the fear of concoction being exposed.

It is contended that accident register extract produced as Ex.R1 established that deceased was brought by one Siddaramaiah with a history of RTA at Yeliyur circle and it was hit by a two wheeler 'not known' and later, the vehicle number was inserted by overwriting.
It is alleged that, the Tribunal ought to have seen that the accident register extract is believable and it has adopted two standards of proof, one for the claimants and another for the insurer.
It is also contended that the fraud and justice do not dwell together and the evidence on record was not properly appreciated by the Tribunal.

The Branch Manager vs Smt Lakshmamma on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169262750/
4 10.

Heard Sri O Mahesh, learned counsel for the appellant-Insurance Company and Sri S.Shanker Shetty, learned counsel for respondent Nos. 1, 3 to 5 and Smt. Mamatha G. Kulkarni, learned counsel for respondent No.6.
Respondent No.2 is dead and respondent No.1, 3 to - 10 - 5 are treated as her LRs vide order dated 5-6-2015 and perused the Tribunal records.
11. The learned counsel appearing for the appellant Sri O Mahesh, submits that the delay of two days in filing the FIR indicates fraud and false implication of the motor cycle.
It is contended that the proper issues have not been framed by the Tribunal and the issues framed are mechanically framed.

It is submitted that the villagers had lodged a complaint to the SP, Mandya as per Ex.R1 indicating that the deceased had sustained injuries while he was travelling on a bullock cart and a branch of the tree hit him causing injuries and later he succumbed to the death.
It is contended that the Ex.R1 is proved by examining the author and the Tribunal has not appreciated the evidence in a proper way.
He contends that there are two FIRs prior to the death and after the death and the accused never appeared before the Criminal court.
He contends that the eye witnesses Jayalingegowda was not examined and this goes to the root of the case.

He relied - 11 - on the decision of the Andhra Pradesh High Court in the case of Konda Anuradha and others Vs.
Gopi Reddy Venkat Reddy and others (ACJ 2009 708) and the decision of the Division Bench of this Court in the case of the Regional Office, United India Insurance Co.,Ltd. Vs. Smt. Gayathridevi and others (MFA 11443/2006 disposed of on 18-7-2012) along with connected matters to buttress his arguments.

Konda Anuradha and others Vs.
Gopi Reddy Venkat Reddy and others (ACJ 2009 708)

sentences.text: I have gone through the above decisions.
In Konda Anuradha case, the police investigation showed that there was no accident and as such it can be distinguished on facts.
So far as Gayatridevi case is concerned, it was a case wherein the police investigation, including the spot panchanama showed that the accident was by unknown vehicle.
In the case on hand, the MLC register showed the vehicle number.
Hence this decision is not applicable.
It is to be noted that there cannot be precedent made applicable regarding the facts.
Precedents are applicable regarding the principles and the ratio.
Per contra, learned counsel appearing for respondents/ claimants submitted that the Tribunal has considered all these aspects argued by the learned counsel for the appellant in the impugned judgment.
It is submitted that there were no specific defences that are raised in the written statement and therefore, framing the issues on such contentions did not arise.
It is submitted that para 17 and 18 of the judgment show that all these contentions raised by the appellants have been considered at length.
13. The first contention of the learned counsel appearing for the appellant is that the proper issues were not framed by the Tribunal.

The perusal of the written statement filed by the respondent No.2 The Branch Manager vs Smt Lakshmamma on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169262750/
5 insurance company before the Tribunal shows that the accident is denied by the insurance company and there are no specific contentions.

In para 8 of the written statement , it was contended that the deceased Chikkalingaiah without observing the vehicle coming on the road, tried to cross - 13 - the road and in that process, he himself dashed against the motor cycle and fell down.
Therefore, the manner in which the accident had occurred was never disputed by the insurance company in its written statement.
Therefore, I do not find any reason to accept this argument that the proper issues were not framed by the Tribunal.
14. The second contention of the learned counsel appearing for the appellant is that, there is a delay of 02 days in filing the complaint which establish concoction of the alleged accident.

The perusal of the complaint at Ex.P2 and the FIR at Ex.P1 shows that Jayalingegowda files the complaint stating that he and deceased Chikkalingaiah were waiting in the Mandya bus stand and they boarded a bus and got down at Yeliyur circle at about 11.30 a.m.
While crossing the road, the Motor cycle came from Mysuru side and dashed to Chikkalingaiah.
The motor cyclist did not stop and went away and motor cycle was bearing KA.09.EN/4671.

When Chikkalingaiah was shifted to Mandya hospital, he was advised to take him to - 14 - NIMHANS and accordingly, he informed his villagers and after arrival of Siddarama and Lokesh,
the injured Chikkalingaiah was shifted to NIMHANS and returned on the next day and Chikkalingaiah was admitted to district hospital Mandya.
The said complaint was filed on 11-8- 2009.
Thereafter, the deceased died on 19-9-2009 at Maharaja Agrasena hospital due to the accidental injuries and as such, the offence under Section 304A of IPC was included.
It is evident that there are no such two FIRs as contended by the insurance company.
Ultimately, the chargesheet was filed by the investigating officer.
15. There is proper explanation which has been offered in the complaint at Ex.P2 and there is no reason to doubt the veracity of Ex.P2 by its bare perusal.

16. Here it is relevant to mention about the decision rendered by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Ravi vs.
Badrinarayan and Others1, wherein it was held that delay in lodging the FIR cannot be a main ground for (2011) 4 SCC 693 - 15 - rejecting the claim and it is the cumulative effect of events which are to be judged.
17.

Further, in the case of Ravi and Others vs. Thammanna and Others2 rendered by this Court, it was also noticed that so far as claim is concerned, a certificate issued in Form No.54 of Rules would suffice to fasten liability on insurance company.

sentences.text:
It was held that there was no necessity for the The Branch Manager vs Smt Lakshmamma on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169262750/
6 petitioner claimant either to prove the FIR or the charge sheet as required under law.

sentences.text: On the other hand, it was for the insurance company which has to prove that the FIR or the charge sheet as incorrect.

18. The Tribunal on its part has considered the material placed before it and ultimately, it came to the conclusion that the petitioners have proved the accident has taken place involving the vehicle owned by respondent No. 1 and insured by respondent No.2 When this Court also comes to the conclusion that the accident is proved to have happened by the vehicle owned by respondent No.1 MANU/KA/1124/2021 - 16 - and when there is no cogent evidence to dislodge the same, there are no reason to differ with the conclusion reached by the Tribunal.
Therefore, the challenge by the insurance company regarding the liability has to be rejected.
19. It is necessary to consider the other contentions of the appellant:
The learned counsel for the appellant contended that its own investigator came to know that the alleged accident is concocted.

The officer of the respondent No.2 contended that one Gangadharaiah son of Thamburi Boraiah had lodged a complaint on 6-9-2011 to SP, Mandya, that the deceased was working in the Jaggery plant of one Shivaramu and on 9-8-2009 while the sugarcane was being transported to the plant in a bullock cart, a branch of the tree over the road hit on the neck of the deceased and he fell down and sustained injuries and later died in the hospital.
Thereafter, SP, Mandya, informed the same to the insurance company and as per - 17 - the instructions by the SP, Mandya, a complaint was filed by him on 12-7-2012 and it was investigated by Mandya Rural police by registering an FIR for the offences under Sections 415, 420 of IPC.

He further contended and produced Ex.R1 to show that initially, the vehicle number was not mentioned in the MLC register and later, the word 'not known' was struck off and the vehicle number was inserted.
20.

Obviously, the contentions stated by RW1 were not part of the written statement and therefore,
the question of framing of an issue in this regard did not arise before the Tribunal.
It is relevant to note that the said complaint filed by the insurance company before the Mandya Rural Police is produced at Ex.R5 and Ex.R6.
It is accompanied by an alleged letter by Gangadharaiah son of Thamburi Boraiah and few others.
It is on a bond paper of Rs.2/- wherein, certain allegations were made stating that several false cases have been field and MVC 225/2010 is a false case and there was no such accident.

Allegations - 18 - The Branch Manager vs Smt Lakshmamma on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169262750/
7 were made against the advocates, jaggery plant owners and the police.

21. The Ex.R4 is the letter by the SP, Mandya, which states that some villagers had filed a complaint on 6-9- 2011 and the preliminary enquiry showed that they were true and therefore, suitable complaint may be filed with the relevant documents.
22. Accordingly the insurance company filed a complaint and the said complaint was investigated by the Dy.SP, and ultimately, he submitted a report after examining about 17 witnesses as per Ex.P11.

In Ex.P11, it was stated that the applicants 1 to 4, who had signed the complaint to the SP as per Ex.R7, had retracted saying that their signatures were obtained by Gangadharaiah under the guise of submitting the representation to the Panchayath for the road repairs.
The applicants 5 to 14 had stated that the deceased Chikkalingaiah had sustained RTA at Yeliyur circle and later died due to the injuries.
The applicants at Sl.No.15 and 16 had stated that - 19 - Chikkalingaiah had died wile he was transporting the sugar cane but not by a RTA.
The report also stated that the medical officer Dr. Habeed Khan had stated that one Siddaram had brought the injured to the hospital at 1.38 p.m. informing the RTA with the motor cycle.
The Dy.SP did not find any discrepancies in the MLC records.
Ultimately, he concluded that it was a RTA involving the motor cycle bearing No.KA.09.EN 4671 and that the applicant Gangadharaiah had not appeared before him.
23. Thus, it is evident that the allegation of the Insurance Company that it was a concocted accident was also investigated by the Police officer of the rank of Dy.SP.
Hence, the contention of the insurance company that there was no such accident cannot e accepted.

Moreover, it is also relevant to note that the said Gangadharaiah son of Thamburi Boraiah was in enimical terms with the deceased Chikkalingaiah on account of a civil dispute as may be seen from ex.P10, which is the judgment in OS No.214/2007.
It is also relevant to note that the report of - 20 - the private investigator of the insurance company and the documents are at Ex.R9 to 12.
The report is dated 31-8- 2013.

It shows that the owner of the vehicle Ramakrishna was not available in the address given to the insurance company but he came to know that the motor cycle was being used at K. Goudagere and the owner of the jaggery plant Shivaram was using the same.
But there was no material to show that Shivaram was using the said vehicle.
In the course of his investigation, he had recorded the statements of two witnesses as per Ex.R10 and R.11.
Obviously, these documents are of the year 2013.
24. In view of the above evidence on record, it is evident that there is no reason to disbelieve the report of the investigating officer of the rank of Dy.S.P. as per Ex.P11.

The applicants who had submitted the representation to SP, Mandya, had not appeared to give their statements and also that the representation submitted to the SP appears to be concocted as it is on a stamp paper but not in The Branch Manager vs Smt Lakshmamma on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169262750/
8
the form of an affidavit.

Except,
- 21 - Gangadharaiah, majority of others had not supported the aid representation at Ex.R7.
Therefore, it is not possible to hold that there was no such accident as contended by the appellant Insurance Company.
Even if we accept the MLC records as produced at Ex.R1, the veracity of the same was examined by the Dy.SP as may be seen from Ex.P11.
Therefore, simply because there was striking off the word 'unknown' and inserting of the 'vehicle number' in Ex.R1, it cannot be said that there was no such accident.
The final investigation report show that the chargesheet against the rider of the motor cycle is not proved to be false.
25. In that view of the matter, the observations made by the Tribunal that the petitioners had proved the accident has to be accepted.
The Tribunal has considered all the contentions of the appellant herein and came to the conclusion that the accident has been established.
It cannot be said that non examination of Jayalingegowda has resulted in not proving the case of the petitioners.

. Coming to the contention of the learned counsel for he appellant that the secondary evidence produced by the petitioners has been accepted and that of insurance company has been rejected by the Tribunal is concerned, it is to be observed that the proceedings under Section 166 of MV Act, is summary in nature.

The strict rules of evidence are not applicable inasmuch as, the Motor Vehicles Act, prescribes that as soon as an information of the vehicular accident is reported, the Tribunal has to initiate the proceedings under Section 166 of MV Act, and it is for the Insurance Company to establish its contentions.
Obviously, the Insurance company has come up with the contention that there was no such accident belatedly, at the time of the evidence.
The contentions that the deceased sustained injuries while transporting the sugarcane to the jaggery plant never found a place in the written statement.
Therefore, it is evident that the contentions were raised on the basis of the certain representations by the people who were enimical towards the deceased or his employer.

Under these circumstances,
- 23 - no fault can be found with the observations made by the Tribunal.

It is evident that the history of road traffic accident mentioned in Ex.R1, which came into existence out of spontaneity at about 1.30 p.m. on the date of the accident, is not falsified by any cogent evidence.
The representation by some villagers after three years after the incident cannot in any way be accepted as rebuttal of Ex.R1.
The Tribunal has considered these aspects in para 17 to 20 of the impugned judgment.
In that view of the matter, I do not find any merits in the appeal.
27. For the reasons aforesaid, the appeal deserves to be dismissed.

Hence, the following:
The Branch Manager vs Smt Lakshmamma on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169262750/
9 ORDER
The appeal filed by the Insurance Company is dismissed.
The amount in deposit, if any, shall be transmitted to the jurisdictional Tribunal, forthwith.

Sd/-
JUDGE

The representation by some villagers after three years after the incident cannot in any way be accepted as rebuttal of Ex.R1.
